I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this is the safest and steadiest way for me to protect yield, use my irrigation water carefully, and keep the work rhythm familiar. I would not spread myself across too many crops. At my age and with my experience, I would rather plant crops I know well, use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put fertilizer in at moderate but reliable levels, and aim for stable output instead of taking extra market or weather risk.

For wheat, I will focus on strong seedling establishment, one good base fertilizer application, then topdress nitrogen around jointing, irrigate at the key stages, and control aphids and rust if pressure shows up. After wheat harvest, I will move directly into summer maize on the same land so I do not lose moisture or time. For maize, I will sow quickly after harvest, keep planting density even, give nitrogen mainly at the big flare stage, irrigate when the field really needs it, and control weeds and corn borer in time. I will keep tillage simple: plough before wheat to prepare the land well, then use no-tillage or minimal disturbance before maize so I can save labor and catch the season.
